question: Carlos is planting a lemon tree. The tree will cost $90 to plant. Each year it will grow 7 lemons, which he can sell for $1.5 each. It costs $3 a year to water and feed the tree. How many years will it take before he starts earning money on the lemon tree?

Cost per year (water and feed) = $3.00.
Annual net income = Revenue - Cost = $10.50 - $3.00 = $7.50.<|llm_offload|>

To find out how many years it will take before Carlos starts earning money on the lemon tree, we need to calculate his annual profit and then determine how many years it will take to cover the initial cost.

1. **Calculate the annual revenue:**
   The tree grows 7 lemons each year, and Carlos can sell them for $1.50 each.
   Annual revenue = 7 lemons * $1.50/lemon = $10.50

2. **Calculate the annual profit:**
   It costs $3.00 a year to water and feed the tree. We subtract this cost from the annual revenue to find the annual profit.
   Annual profit = $10.50 (revenue) - $3.00 (cost) = $7.50

3. **Calculate the time to break even:**
   The initial cost to plant the tree is $90. We divide this initial cost by the annual profit to see how many years it will take to recover the cost.
   Years to break even = $90 / $7.50 per year = 12 years

After 12 years, Carlos will have completely paid off the initial $90 cost. Therefore, it will take 12 years before he starts earning money on the lemon tree.

\boxed{12}

To determine how many years it will take for Carlos to start earning money (break even), we need to calculate his annual net profit and divide the initial cost by that amount.

**Step 1: Calculate the annual revenue.**
Carlos sells 7 lemons per year at a price of $1.50 each.
$$7 \text{ lemons} \times \$1.50/\text{lemon} = \$10.50$$
So, the tree generates $\$10.50$ in revenue per year.

**Step 2: Calculate the annual net profit.**
We must subtract the annual cost of watering and feeding the tree from the revenue.
$$\$10.50 \text{ (revenue)} - \$3.00 \text{ (cost)} = \$7.50$$
Carlos makes a net profit of $\$7.50$ per year.

**Step 3: Calculate the number of years to break even.**
The tree cost $\$90$ to plant. We divide the total cost by the annual net profit to find out how many years it takes to recover that cost.
$$\$90 \text{ (initial cost)} \div \$7.50 \text{ (annual profit)} = 12 \text{ years}$$

It will take Carlos 12 years to recover his initial investment.
